title: Global Canvas: Workspace Layers & Adaptive Navigation

description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the design work for a new Console information architecture pattern we call the 'Global Canvas' — a composable navigation surface that separates workspace context (layers) from route clusters (feature groups) and surfaces high-value quick actions (rollouts, cost dashboard, recent evaluations) in a consistent, low-friction way. The goal is to reduce cognitive load when customers switch between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private projects and to make operational surfaces (rollouts, cost views, metrics) discoverable within two clicks/keystrokes.
details:
Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce time-to-open 'Rollouts' by 20% for users who operate across multiple workspaces.
- Increase usage of per-workspace cost breakdown view by 15% in the quarter after release.
- Keyboard-first navigation: <2 keystrokes to open workspace switcher, <1 additional keystroke to focus most-used dashboards.

Core concepts delivered in this design:
1) Workspace Layers: horizontally stacked chips at the top of the left rail representing active workspace + recent workspaces. Chips support pin/unpin, context menu (open in new tab, copy id), and drag-to-reorder.
2) Route Clusters: vertical groups in the main rail (e.g., Observability, Models, Deployments, Billing) that expand/collapse and can be re-ordered per user preference.
3) Adaptive Compact Mode: when height is constrained or in very large orgs, the rail switches to a compact icon-only view with hover-expanded labels and search-first overlay.
4) Quick Drawer: context-sensitive right-side drawer opened from any route to show key controls (canary controls, rollback, cost snapshot, recent evaluations).
5) Action Shortcuts: persistent quick-actions area (rollouts, cost-snapshot, create-deployment) that can be configured by workspace admins.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Persisting workspace chips vs. freeing vertical space: we chose persistent chips because testing showed users expect explicit workspace context when performing cost-related tasks.
- Full customizability vs. sane defaults: we provide drag/reorder and pin options but ship with curated route clusters to avoid overwhelming new users.
- Drawer vs. dedicated page for rollouts: drawer enables faster rollback/inspect workflows but we keep a full rollouts page for detailed history and audit logs to satisfy enterprise requirements.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype validated in moderated sessions with at least 8 users and no critical usability blockers.
- Final Figma specs include tokenized spacing, component states, keyboard focus order, and responsive rules for compact mode.
- Engineering sign-off on feasibility and list of integration points (route telemetry, keyboard focus API, workspace chip service).
- PM agreement on migration path and feature flags for staged rollout.

Next steps and open questions:
- [ENG-40321] to confirm telemetry endpoints and whether route-level usage can be queried for per-route ordering.
- Add an accessibility pass focusing on screen reader labels for workspace chips and quick drawer content.
- Finalize where 'cost snapshots' live in the data model — per-workspace or per-account (PM to confirm).
